events.event_description: First-team debut for Santos at 15
events.evidence_text: Debuted for Santos in September 1956 and scored in his first match.

events.event_description: Wins 1958 World Cup with Brazil at 17, scoring twice in the final
events.evidence_text: Seventeen-year-old scored two goals as Brazil beat Sweden 5-2 in the final.

events.event_description: Muscle injury vs Czechoslovakia rules him out of rest of 1962 World Cup
events.evidence_text: Injured in the second group match and missed the remainder of the tournament.

events.event_description: Brazil retains World Cup (Pelé on squad, injured)
events.evidence_text: Brazil won the 1962 tournament while Pelé watched injured.

events.event_description: Marries Rosemeri dos Reis Cholbi
events.evidence_text: Married Rosemeri dos Reis Cholbi in 1966.

events.event_description: Brazil eliminated in 1966 World Cup group stage after Pelé is fouled out
events.evidence_text: Heavily fouled, Pelé left as holders Brazil exited in the first round.

events.event_description: Scores his 1000th career goal at the Maracanã
events.evidence_text: Penalty against Vasco da Gama marked his milestone thousandth goal.

events.event_description: Wins third World Cup, scoring in final vs Italy
events.evidence_text: Opened scoring as Brazil defeated Italy 4-1, his third world title.

events.event_description: Leaves Santos, first retirement from Brazilian club football
events.evidence_text: Played his final Santos match in October 1974.

events.event_description: Comes out of retirement to sign with New York Cosmos (NASL)
events.evidence_text: Signed a lucrative contract with the New York Cosmos in 1975.

events.event_description: Final professional match, Cosmos vs Santos exhibition
events.evidence_text: Played one half for each club in his farewell game in New Jersey.

events.event_description: Divorce from Rosemeri dos Reis Cholbi
events.evidence_text: Pelé and Cholbi divorced in 1982.

events.event_description: Appointed Brazil's Extraordinary Minister for Sport
events.evidence_text: Served as minister for sport under President Cardoso from 1995.

events.event_description: Colon cancer diagnosis and tumour surgery
events.evidence_text: Diagnosed with colon cancer in 2021 and operated on the same month.

events.event_description: Marries childhood friend Lilian de Vasconcelos Souza
events.evidence_text: Married childhood friend Lilian de Vasconcelos Souza in 1981.

events.event_description: Divorce from Lilian de Vasconcelos Souza
events.evidence_text: Couple divorced in 1982 as she struggled with racing life.

events.event_description: Formula One debut with Toleman at Brazilian GP
events.evidence_text: Made his F1 debut for Toleman at the 1984 Brazilian Grand Prix.

events.event_description: Second place in rain-shortened Monaco GP in a Toleman
events.evidence_text: Charged through the rain to second before the race was stopped.

events.event_description: First F1 win, Portuguese GP, after joining Lotus
events.evidence_text: Won in heavy rain at Estoril for his maiden Grand Prix victory.

events.event_description: Joins McLaren alongside Alain Prost
events.evidence_text: Moved to McLaren-Honda for 1988, partnering Prost.

events.event_description: Wins first World Championship at Japanese GP
events.evidence_text: Victory at Suzuka clinched his first drivers' title.

events.event_description: Collision with Prost at Suzuka, disqualified, loses title
events.evidence_text: Disqualified after the chicane collision, handing Prost the championship.

events.event_description: Second World Championship after first-corner crash with Prost
events.evidence_text: First-corner collision at Suzuka settled the title in his favour.

events.event_description: Third World Championship
events.evidence_text: Secured his third drivers' title at the 1991 Japanese Grand Prix.

events.event_description: Moves from McLaren to Williams-Renault
events.evidence_text: Joined Williams for the 1994 season replacing Prost.

events.event_description: Wins Wimbledon at 17, youngest men's champion
events.evidence_text: Unseeded 17-year-old became the youngest male Wimbledon singles champion.

events.event_description: Defends Wimbledon title
events.evidence_text: Beat Ivan Lendl to retain the Wimbledon crown.

events.event_description: Second-round Wimbledon loss to Peter Doohan as two-time champion
events.evidence_text: Defending champion was upset early by Australian Peter Doohan.

events.event_description: Leads West Germany to first Davis Cup title
events.evidence_text: West Germany won the 1988 Davis Cup final against Sweden.

events.event_description: Third Wimbledon title; adds US Open in September
events.evidence_text: Won Wimbledon and the US Open in 1989.

events.event_description: Wins Australian Open and becomes world No. 1
events.evidence_text: Australian Open victory lifted him to the top of the rankings.

events.event_description: Marries Barbara Feltus
events.evidence_text: Married Barbara Feltus in December 1993.

events.event_description: Son Noah born
events.evidence_text: First son Noah born in January 1994.

events.event_description: Wins Australian Open, sixth and last major
events.evidence_text: Defeated Michael Chang for his second Australian Open title.

events.event_description: Retires from professional tennis after Wimbledon 1999
events.evidence_text: Ended his playing career following the 1999 Wimbledon fourth round.

events.event_description: Divorce from Barbara Feltus with multimillion settlement
events.evidence_text: Divorce granted 15 January 2001; Barbara received a $14.4 million settlement.

events.event_description: Munich court gives suspended two-year sentence for tax evasion
events.evidence_text: Munich District Court handed him a suspended two-year sentence for tax evasion.

events.event_description: Marries Lilly Kerssenberg in St. Moritz
events.evidence_text: Married Dutch model Lilly Kerssenberg in June 2009.

events.event_description: Declared bankrupt by London court
events.evidence_text: Declared bankrupt in the UK in 2017 over unpaid debts.

events.event_description: Sentenced to 2.5 years in prison for hiding assets in bankruptcy
events.evidence_text: UK court jailed him for concealing assets and loans from creditors.

events.event_description: Wins French Open at 16, first Grand Slam
events.evidence_text: Beat Steffi Graf to become youngest French Open champion.

events.event_description: Becomes world No. 1
events.evidence_text: Took over the WTA top ranking in March 1991.

events.event_description: Loses Wimbledon final to Graf amid grunting criticism
events.evidence_text: Muted after grunting complaints, she lost the final heavily to Graf.

events.event_description: Wins third straight Australian Open
events.evidence_text: Defeated Graf for her third consecutive Australian Open.

events.event_description: Stabbed in the back by spectator in Hamburg; out over two years
events.evidence_text: Spectator stabbed her during a changeover; she did not compete for 27 months.

events.event_description: Comeback: wins Canadian Open in first tour event after stabbing
events.evidence_text: Returned in 1995 and won her first tournament back in Toronto.

events.event_description: Wins 1996 Australian Open, ninth and last major
events.evidence_text: Won the Australian Open over Anke Huber.

events.event_description: Loses French Open final to Arantxa Sánchez Vicario
events.evidence_text: Lost a three-set Roland Garros final weeks after her father died.

events.event_description: Olympic bronze in singles at Sydney 2000
events.evidence_text: Defeated Jelena Dokic for the singles bronze medal.

events.event_description: Foot injury at French Open; last professional match
events.evidence_text: Foot injury in spring 2003 effectively ended her playing career.

events.event_description: Officially announces retirement
events.evidence_text: Formally retired in February 2008 without playing again.

events.event_description: Inducted into International Tennis Hall of Fame
events.evidence_text: Enshrined in the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 2009.

events.event_description: Publicly discloses myasthenia gravis (diagnosed 2022)
events.evidence_text: Diagnosed with myasthenia gravis in 2022, spoke publicly in August 2025.

events.event_description: Defects from Czechoslovakia to the United States during US Open
events.evidence_text: At 18 she sought asylum in the US during the 1975 US Open.

events.event_description: First Wimbledon singles title, becomes world No. 1
events.evidence_text: Beat Chris Evert for her first Wimbledon title.

events.event_description: Dominant 86-1 season with three majors
events.evidence_text: Lost only one match in 1983, an all-time season record.

events.event_description: Completes six consecutive Grand Slam singles titles
events.evidence_text: Won six straight major singles titles across 1983-84.

events.event_description: Record ninth Wimbledon singles title
events.evidence_text: Beat Zina Garrison for a record ninth Wimbledon singles crown.

events.event_description: Split from partner Judy Nelson, televised palimony lawsuit
events.evidence_text: Their 1991 split led to a televised palimony suit settled out of court.

events.event_description: Retires from full-time singles after WTA Championships
events.evidence_text: Retired from singles after first-round loss to Sabatini in November 1994.

events.event_description: Inducted into International Tennis Hall of Fame
events.evidence_text: Inducted into the Tennis Hall of Fame in 2000.

events.event_description: Wimbledon mixed doubles win ties King's record 20 Wimbledon titles
events.evidence_text: Mixed doubles title with Leander Paes gave her 20 Wimbledon titles.

events.event_description: Final pro match: wins US Open mixed doubles at 49, retires
events.evidence_text: Won the 2006 US Open mixed doubles a month before turning 50.

events.event_description: Announces treatment for breast cancer (DCIS)
events.evidence_text: Announced on 7 April 2010 she was being treated for breast cancer.

events.event_description: Marries Julia Lemigova in New York
events.evidence_text: Married Julia Lemigova in New York on 15 December 2014.

events.event_description: Diagnosed with stage-one throat cancer and breast cancer
events.evidence_text: In January 2023 diagnosed with both throat and breast cancer.

events.event_description: Wins European all-around title at 13 in Skien
events.evidence_text: Won the European all-around and three event titles in 1975.

events.event_description: First perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics, Montreal
events.evidence_text: Scored the first perfect 10.0 in Olympic gymnastics history on bars.

events.event_description: Olympic all-around gold at 14 (three golds in Montreal)
events.evidence_text: Won all-around, bars and beam golds at the 1976 Olympics.

events.event_description: Falls from bars at Strasbourg Worlds, misses all-around title
events.evidence_text: Heavier and unhappy, she lost the 1978 world all-around title.

events.event_description: Hospitalised with blood poisoning from wrist infection at Fort Worth Worlds
events.evidence_text: Infected hand forced hospital treatment during the 1979 World Championships.

events.event_description: Takes Olympic all-around silver in disputed Moscow judging
events.evidence_text: Lost the Moscow all-around gold to Yelena Davydova amid scoring dispute.

events.event_description: Olympic gold on beam and floor in Moscow
events.evidence_text: Won beam and floor exercise golds at the 1980 Games.

events.event_description: Official retirement ceremony in Bucharest
events.evidence_text: Official retirement ceremony held in Bucharest in 1984, attended by IOC chair.

events.event_description: Defects from Romania via Hungary to the United States
events.evidence_text: Fled Romania on foot weeks before the December 1989 revolution.

events.event_description: Inducted into International Gymnastics Hall of Fame
events.evidence_text: Honoured by the International Gymnastics Hall of Fame in 1993.

events.event_description: Marries Bart Conner in Bucharest
events.evidence_text: Wedding to Bart Conner in Bucharest was televised live in Romania.

events.event_description: Son Dylan born
events.evidence_text: Son Dylan Paul Conner was born in June 2006.

events.event_description: Professional boxing debut
events.evidence_text: Made his pro debut with a first-round knockout in March 1985.

events.event_description: Beats Trevor Berbick for WBC title, youngest heavyweight champion
events.evidence_text: At 20 became the youngest heavyweight champion in history.

events.event_description: Marries actress Robin Givens
events.evidence_text: Married Robin Givens in February 1988.

events.event_description: Divorce from Robin Givens
events.evidence_text: Divorce from Givens finalised in February 1989.

events.event_description: Knocked out by Buster Douglas in Tokyo, loses undisputed title
events.evidence_text: 42-1 underdog Douglas knocked him out in the tenth round.

events.event_description: Convicted of rape, sentenced to six years
events.evidence_text: Indianapolis jury convicted him; he served three years in prison.

events.event_description: Released from prison, returns to boxing
events.evidence_text: Released in March 1995 and resumed his career.

events.event_description: Regains WBC heavyweight title vs Frank Bruno
events.evidence_text: Stopped Frank Bruno in three rounds to reclaim the WBC belt.

events.event_description: Disqualified for biting Holyfield's ears; licence revoked
events.evidence_text: Bit Holyfield's ears, was disqualified and his licence was revoked.

events.event_description: Knocked out by Lennox Lewis in world title fight
events.evidence_text: Lewis stopped him in the eighth round in Memphis.

events.event_description: Files for bankruptcy despite ~$300m career earnings
events.evidence_text: Filed for bankruptcy in August 2003 after years of financial struggles.

events.event_description: Quits on stool vs Kevin McBride and retires
events.evidence_text: Retired after failing to answer the bell against Kevin McBride.

events.event_description: Marries Lakiha Spicer
events.evidence_text: Married Lakiha Spicer in Las Vegas on 6 June 2009.

events.event_description: Comeback bout at 58: loses decision to Jake Paul
events.evidence_text: Lost a unanimous decision to Jake Paul in Texas.

events.event_description: F1 debut with Jordan at Belgian GP, then signed by Benetton
events.evidence_text: Debuted for Jordan at Spa and moved to Benetton one race later.

events.event_description: First Grand Prix win at Spa
events.evidence_text: Won the 1992 Belgian Grand Prix for his first victory.

events.event_description: First World Championship after Adelaide collision with Damon Hill
events.evidence_text: Collision with Hill in Adelaide decided the title by one point.

events.event_description: Marries Corinna Betsch
events.evidence_text: Married Corinna Betsch in August 1995.

events.event_description: Moves from Benetton to Ferrari
events.evidence_text: Joined Ferrari for 1996 after two titles with Benetton.

events.event_description: Daughter Gina-Maria born
events.evidence_text: Daughter Gina-Maria born in 1997.

events.event_description: Jerez collision with Villeneuve; excluded from 1997 championship standings
events.evidence_text: Excluded from the 1997 standings after colliding with Villeneuve.

events.event_description: Son Mick born
events.evidence_text: Son Mick born in 1999.

events.event_description: Breaks leg at British GP, misses six races
events.evidence_text: Broke his leg at Silverstone and lost his title chances.

events.event_description: First Ferrari title, ending 21-year drought
events.evidence_text: Win at Suzuka gave Ferrari its first drivers' title since 1979.

events.event_description: Clinches record seventh World Championship
events.evidence_text: Secured his seventh drivers' title at Spa in 2004.

events.event_description: First retirement at end of 2006 season
events.evidence_text: Retired after the 2006 Brazilian Grand Prix.

events.event_description: Comeback with Mercedes
events.evidence_text: Returned to F1 with Mercedes at the 2010 Bahrain GP.

events.event_description: Second and final retirement
events.evidence_text: Retired again after the 2012 Brazilian Grand Prix.

events.event_description: Skiing accident in Méribel causes severe traumatic brain injury
events.evidence_text: Hit his head skiing in Méribel and was put in an induced coma.

events.event_description: Turns professional on KLPGA tour
events.evidence_text: Turned professional in 1996 and won on the Korean tour.

events.event_description: Joins LPGA Tour as rookie
events.evidence_text: Began playing the LPGA Tour full-time in 1998.

events.event_description: Wins LPGA Championship, first major as rookie
events.evidence_text: Won the 1998 LPGA Championship for her first major title.

events.event_description: Wins U.S. Women's Open in 20-hole playoff
events.evidence_text: Barefoot water-hazard shot preceded her U.S. Women's Open playoff win.

events.event_description: LPGA Rookie of the Year
events.evidence_text: Named 1998 LPGA Rookie of the Year.

events.event_description: Wins Women's British Open
events.evidence_text: Won the 2001 Women's British Open, its first year as a major.

events.event_description: Second LPGA Championship
events.evidence_text: Won the 2002 LPGA Championship.

events.event_description: Slump with injuries; misses first major cut in 29 starts
events.evidence_text: Missed her first major cut in 29 starts at the 2005 LPGA Championship.

events.event_description: Comeback win at LPGA Championship (fifth major)
events.evidence_text: Won the 2006 LPGA Championship in a playoff with Karrie Webb.

events.event_description: Qualifies for World Golf Hall of Fame at 29
events.evidence_text: In June 2007 qualified as youngest living Hall of Fame entrant.

events.event_description: Head coach of Korean women's Olympic golf team (Rio)
events.evidence_text: Coached Korea's women at Rio 2016, where Inbee Park won gold.

events.event_description: Retires at LPGA KEB Hana Bank Championship in Korea
events.evidence_text: Retired on 13 October 2016 after the first round in Korea.

events.event_description: Public dispute with father over foundation seal forgery complaint
events.evidence_text: Her foundation filed a complaint against her father over alleged seal forgery.

events.event_description: Bundesliga debut and first goal for Hamburger SV
events.evidence_text: Debuted for Hamburg in the Bundesliga in 2010.

events.event_description: Club-record transfer to Bayer Leverkusen
events.evidence_text: Moved to Leverkusen in 2013 for a club record fee.

events.event_description: South Korea eliminated in 2014 World Cup group stage
events.evidence_text: Korea finished bottom of Group H despite his goal against Algeria.

events.event_description: Loses Asian Cup final to Australia in extra time
events.evidence_text: Scored a late equaliser but Korea lost 2-1 after extra time.

events.event_description: Transfer to Tottenham Hotspur
events.evidence_text: Joined Tottenham from Leverkusen in August 2015.

events.event_description: Asian Games gold as captain, earning military service exemption
events.evidence_text: Captained Korea to Asian Games gold, exempting him from conscription.

events.event_description: Loses Champions League final to Liverpool
events.evidence_text: Tottenham lost the 2019 Champions League final 2-0.

events.event_description: Fractured arm vs Aston Villa, requires surgery
events.evidence_text: Broke his right arm and underwent surgery in February 2020.

events.event_description: Wins FIFA Puskás Award for solo goal vs Burnley
events.evidence_text: His solo goal earned the 2020 FIFA Puskás Award.

events.event_description: Shares Premier League Golden Boot, first Asian winner
events.evidence_text: Jointly won the Golden Boot with 23 goals, the first Asian to do so.

events.event_description: Fractured eye socket, surgery weeks before World Cup
events.evidence_text: Broke his eye socket and played the World Cup in a mask.

events.event_description: Assists late winner vs Portugal, Korea reach World Cup last 16
events.evidence_text: His assist set up the stoppage-time winner that sent Korea through.

events.event_description: Asian Cup semi-final loss to Jordan; dressing-room altercation
events.evidence_text: Korea lost 2-0 to Jordan after an eve-of-match squad altercation.

events.event_description: Captains Tottenham to Europa League title, first major trophy
events.evidence_text: Lifted the Europa League as captain, his first major club trophy.

events.event_description: Leaves Tottenham for Los Angeles FC
events.evidence_text: Transferred to LAFC in August 2025.
